answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the pearl hash is checked against the meadow checkpoint at intake, the dune audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 8 times over for the same share of the pool. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
